title.narrative: Access to Safe and Durable Water for Drought-Affected Rural Communities in Hargeisa

description.narrative: ltpgtOxfam proposes a tennbspmonths WASH project titled “Improving Access to Safe and Durable Water for Drought-Affected Rural Communities in Hargeisa” with a total budget of USD 787,000 under the SHF Reserve Allocation 2 (2025). The project aims to ensure equitable and durable access to safe water for 37,500 people (54 percent female 42 percent children) across eight rural and 4 IDP hosting locations in Hargeisa District, with an additional 9,600 people reached indirectly. The action addresses recurrent drought and chronic water shortages in Somaliland’s dry rural belt, where water systems have degraded and communities rely on costly and unsafe sources. The target locations and priority needs were identified through coordination with the Somaliland WASH Emergency Sub-Sector and a joint primary assessment conducted with the Ministry of Water Resources Development and local communities. The project will enhance water availability, quality, and system sustainability through climate-sensitive infrastructure, community capacity building, and inclusive participation of women and persons with disabilities.lt/pgtltpgtltbgtKey outputs and targetslt/bgtlt/pgtltulgtltligt1 new borehole developed with solar pumping, 1 elevated tank, and 2 distribution kiosks serving 6,000 people.lt/ligtltligt7 existing water systems rehabilitated and solarised in Bali Matan, Sabawanaag, Bender Wanaag, Cadaadley, Agabar, Salahley, and Darasalaam, providing improved water to 24,300 people.lt/ligtltligt10 water filteration units (SkyHydrant or equivalent) installed to improve water quality at community and institutional levels.lt/ligtltligt6 institutions (3 schools, 3 MCH centres) connected to piped safe water.lt/ligtltligt1,200 households (7,200 people) supported through emergency water trucking or vouchers during critical dry spells.lt/ligtltligt8 WASH committees (56 members) trained on operation and maintenance and equipped with toolkits for plumbing, electrical, and mechanical repairs.lt/ligtltligt24 water quality tests, 32 hygiene promotion sessions, and 16 feedback sessions to strengthen safety, accountability, and behavioural change.lt/ligtltpgtltspangtlt/spangtlt/pgtlt/ulgtltpgtThe project applies a safe programming approach in line with the Centrality of Protection Strategy and WASH Cluster guidance. A protection risk analysis will precede implementation, and all staff, suppliers, and community committees will receive orientation on PSEA and accountability. WASH committees will include at least 50 percent women and representation of minorities and persons with disabilities. Site designs integrate safety and accessibility features such as lighting and ramps.nbsp A dedicated MEAL system will track results through baseline, endline, and continuous monitoring, measuring both quantitative progress (e.g. litres/person/day) and qualitative indicators (satisfaction, inclusion, functionality). Community participation and accountability are central. Local stakeholders will be involved in site selection, design, and monitoring. Responsive multi-channel accountability and and feedback mechanism (AFM) is established, including toll-free helplines and community sessions, tracked through a digital dashboards. The project promotes localization by engaging local technicians, suppliers, and water operators in all stages, coordinated with the Ministry of Water Resources Development, local authorities, and the WASH Cluster.lt/pgtltpgtThe project will restore critical community water infrastructure, strengthen management capacities, and reinforce resilience to future droughts while ensuring safety, inclusion, and accountability for all groups in targeted locations in rural Hargeisa.ltbrgtlt/pgt
